findings.F1: In coins whose 90-day return is 0 or above, the 5-day excess return after an up day grows with the rise's size in usual 20-day moves: +2.18 % (t 2.25, 149 grid cases) for 1 to 2 moves, +3.67 % (t 2.32, 43) for 2 to 3, and +7.28 % (t 1.85, 27) above 3. The slope of the 5-day excess return on the rise over all up days is +0.0138 per usual move (t 3.08, 751 cases).
findings.F2: These rising-market rises of more than one usual move have a strength of 0.267 of the coin's usual 5-day move (t 3.64, 219 cases), about 2.8 % per case, roughly 15 times the 0.19 % cost of a trade. They are positive in all six coins (t from 0.38 for LTC to 2.21 for ZEC) and in 7 of 8 years (only 2022 is negative, with 6 cases).

ideas.idea: In one coin whose 90-day return is positive, the larger the day's rise measured in usual daily moves of its last 20 days, the higher the coin's return over the next 5 days.
ideas.consequence: A sharp rise in a rising coin is a reason to buy for the following days rather than to fade it, and more so the sharper the rise.
ideas.name: sharp rises extend uptrends

ideas.idea: In one coin, after a one-day rise of several usual daily moves, the lower its 20-day volatility relative to its 60-day volatility, the higher its return over the next 5 days.
ideas.consequence: A sharp rise that breaks out of a quiet stretch is a stronger reason to buy than the same rise in an already agitated market.
ideas.name: quiet-market breakouts continue

ideas.idea: In one coin, the larger the day's fall measured in usual daily moves of its last 20 days, the higher its return over the next 1 day.
ideas.consequence: A sharp down day is a reason to take a short-lived long position for the following day, not to chase the fall.
ideas.name: sharp falls rebound next day
